insights.title: More very hot days
insights.body: Days at 35 °C or hotter went from about 4 to 9 a year. Heat at flowering cuts yields of rice, maize and most pulses.

insights.title: Rain is more than crops can use
insights.body: Rain exceeds crop water demand by about 440 mm a year. Waterlogging and runoff are bigger risks than drought.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area
insights.body: Oil palm, Rubber and Cashew score highest on climate, water and soil fit.

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: In a dry year, rain can drop to about 1,413 mm
consequences.detail: That is 20% below the 1,770 mm average; about 1 year in 10 is this dry or worse.
consequences.action: Keep a drought-tolerant crop in the plan as insurance.

consequences.headline: +0.7 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 26.5 °C to about 27.2 °C. Most recommended crops stay inside their temperature range.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.
